problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\frac{\sqrt{5}s}{3}⟩,\,0\le s\le 4\pi .
$$
worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}s}{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{1}{3}|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{2})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{2})+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
